text:
jena: Heads-up: new contributors hitting the onboarding sample are seeing tons of noisy debug logs when OpenTelemetry is enabled. Also noticed some request lines missing req_id and one header leaked an email.

leo: Oof. Which sample branch and how to repro?

jena: Branch `onboard/telemetry-v2`. Steps: `git checkout onboard/telemetry-v2 && ./dev up --with-telemetry && ./dev logs`. Minimal snippet: 
```
2026-03-25T14:20:11.001Z INFO app server ready
2026-03-25T14:20:11.123Z DEBUG netlib initiating request to /v1/embed
2026-03-25T14:20:11.124Z DEBUG netlib raw-headers: Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX user:zoe@example.com
2026-03-25T14:20:11.125Z WARN telemetry req_id not found for outgoing request
```
jena: The token is redacted but `user:zoe@example.com` shows up. Happens even if I set `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info` sometimes because internal debug from `netlib` prints before our wrapper scrubs.

leo: Are we running the sample with an older SDK pin? We changed hook ordering in 0.9.1 to ensure logging injection runs before OTLP exporter in some modes.

jena: package.json shows `redwood-sdk@0.8.5`. Also the env here has `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first` because I was experimenting.

ops-bot: Note: related SDK change landed in https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/428 (hook ordering + header scrub enhancements).

leo: Okay. Short fixes: (1) bump sample to ^0.9.1 so injectors run consistently, (2) add a defensive header scrub as early as possible in the fetch wrapper to sanitize any email-like or token-like patterns, (3) add a small integration test that runs the sample with `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first` and asserts logs don't contain email regex matches, (4) update quickstart docs to recommend `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info` for first-run.

jena: I tried swapping to `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=logging_first` and it reduces missing req_id lines but didn't eliminate the raw header leak because `netlib` logs its own internal debug before our wrapper.

leo: For the raw debug we should either: (a) put a tiny shim in `node_modules/netlib`? No. (b) intercept stdout/stderr for the child process? brittle. (c) add normalization in the earliest possible layer: the HTTP primitive used by netlib. We already wrap fetch; ensure the wrapper normalizes headers and strings before any call to underlying lib that might log them.

jena: Agreed. I'll prototype a `normalizeAndScrubHeaders(headers)` that replaces emails with `<redacted_email>` and tokens with `<redacted_token>`. We'll keep it toggleable via `REDWOOD_SCRUB_STRICT=true` for low-risk rollout.

leo: Please also make sure we don't double-redact (e.g., `Bearer <redacted_token>` should remain single-tagged). Add unit tests for that case.

ci-bot: CI triggered: branch jena/telemetry-scrub-proto. Jobs: lint, unit, integration (logs-scan).

jena: I'll add a README blurb: "If you see many DEBUG network logs or missing req_id in debug lines, try setting REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info or upgrading the sample SDK. If you need OTEL-first ordering for experimentation, enable REDWOOD_SCRUB_STRICT to ensure headers are sanitized before any debug paths."

leo: Also add a small troubleshooting note: how to verify req_id propagation by grepping logs for `req_id=` and showing an example golden line. That helps support triage.

jena: Will do. Planning to land the scrubbing PR on a feature branch behind a feature flag so we can monitor for false positives.

leo: Thanks — after PR lands I'll run quick e2e with `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first` to validate.

jena: One more ask: can someone add an integration CI assertion that fails if any log line matches common PII regexes (emails, SSNs) for the sample app? The integration should run in CI with redaction flags off and on so it catches regressions.

ops-bot: Suggestion logged: #infra-ticket-991 for adding logs-scan step across onboarding samples.

jena: Great. Leaving the dev instance running until we confirm scrub works. Thanks all :rocket:
